original_card.question: Which unresolved physical correction, endpoint transport or hosting obligation in a pinned P104 follow-up can be closed or decisively rejected?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the P104 row in research-family-status.md and its exact pending source heads before choosing a task. #1991 is the reviewed channel; #2586 is a pending physical dual with explicit added transport costs, not an admitted supplier.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live claims, pin the chosen follow-up and reproduce only the evidence needed for one unresolved obligation. Compare its complete correction/transport/hosting invoice with the target budget; test legal chronological access. Do not rebuild #1991 or assume #2586 has solved global admission.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.

actual_scope: Re-optimize pending PR2920's two-history P104 price (head b9ea9def) with the added constraint C+U >= L for the reported X-only lifetime floors 216/219/234 and the 387 relay estimate; certify each optimizer, moment and root bracket, and the first rejecting floor.
scope_change_reason: The card asks which pinned P104 follow-up obligation can be closed or rejected. The newest follow-up, PR2920, prices its route at 208 lifetimes, below written floors reported in the same model. This audit closes that pricing inconsistency for one pinned follow-up instead of building a new correction.
bottleneck_link: Decides whether known lifetime floors reject the cheapest remaining restricted P104 side-correction route (they do not), and gives the floor (423) that would.
stop_rule: Stop after certifying the optimum for each reported floor and the first rejecting floor; do not search new histories or constructions.
evidence: verify.py emits PASS_P104_TWO_HISTORY_LIFETIME_FLOOR with pr2920_curve_checked=True; test_verify.py passes the positive case and 6 controls (CPython 3.13.16 and 3.12, Linux, 2026-10-16).
author: Sudarsh Chaturvedi
ai_assistance: Anthropic Claude (Opus 5.5) found the gap, wrote the checker, controls and README; the author directed the session.
